title: Journey - Five Days of Peace - Day 2: Cast your cares

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Peace. <short pause> This is day two, Cast Your Cares. <short pause> Our first step was to turn our palms up and show God the worry, with three words... here it is. <short pause> Today we learn what can happen next.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let's settle. <short pause> Notice your shoulders, and how high they've climbed. <short pause> You don't need to pull them down. <short pause> Just notice them, the way you might notice someone standing in a doorway with their coat still on. <short pause> Breathe in easily... <short pause> and breathe out.

There is a kind of worry that we don't hold in our hands at all. <short pause> We wear it. <short pause> It goes on in the morning with our clothes. <short pause> It gets heavy, like wool in the rain. <short pause> And after a while we stop feeling it as a thing we put on... and begin to think it is simply who we are.

The apostle Peter wrote to believers who had plenty of reasons to be worried. <short pause> They were scattered, misunderstood, and suffering for their faith. <short pause> He doesn't tell them their cares are imaginary. <short pause> He tells them what to do with them, and why, in his first letter, chapter five, verse seven.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

That word for casting turns up in one other story. <short pause> When Jesus rode toward Jerusalem, His friends took off their cloaks and threw them over the back of a young donkey. <short pause> It's the same word. <short pause> They didn't hold on to a sleeve. <short pause> The cloak left their shoulders... and something else carried it up the road.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: But listen to the reason Peter gives. <short pause> It isn't, because worry is wrong. <short pause> It isn't, because you ought to be stronger. <short pause> It is because He cares for you. <short pause> Before you are someone with a problem, you are someone He is fond of. <short pause> The coat matters to Him, because of who has been shivering inside it.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So let's take it off. <short pause> Think of one care that you have been wearing. <short pause> Feel where it sits... across the neck, down the back. <short pause> Now, in your imagination, undo the top button. <short pause> And the next. <short pause> Slip one arm free, and then the other. <short pause> Feel the air where the weight was. <short pause> And lay the whole heavy thing across His arms.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: What is it like to stand there without it, even for a breath? <short pause> Perhaps it's lighter. <short pause> Perhaps you feel bare, and you want it back. <short pause> Either one is all right. <short pause> Let Him look at you for a moment... not at the coat. <short pause> At you.

parts.style: tender reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: You may find it on your shoulders again by supper time. <short pause> That isn't weak faith. <short pause> It's a long habit, and you can take it off as often as you notice. <short pause> And giving God your care never means giving up your medicine, or your treatment, or the people helping you. <short pause> Those may be some of the ways that He is caring.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is our second step, after the first. <short pause> Palms up... here it is. <short pause> Now let your shoulders drop, just a little, as if a coat were sliding from them... and say, <short pause> it's Yours. <short pause> Both together, slowly. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> It's Yours.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Let's pray. <short pause> Father, I have worn this for so long. <short pause> I take it off in front of You, and I ask You to carry what I was never made to wear. <short pause> Thank You that You care about the care... and that You care far more for me. <short pause> Teach my shoulders to believe it. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: warm, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: For the rest of today, let every coat you see remind you. <short pause> One on a hook, one over a chair, one on a stranger at the crossing. <short pause> Drop your shoulders, and say it under your breath... <short pause> it's Yours. <short pause> Go lightly.
